title: Your phone
intro: Your phone already knows too much about you. I just want the highlights.

cards.prompt: The main group chat is at 99+ unread. Be honest. In there, you're the…

options.t: Planner. "Saturday, 7pm, I already booked it."
Recruiter. "Everyone, this is Sam. Be nice."
Courier. Screenshots the good stuff straight to my two favorites.
Ghost. Reads everything, says nothing, still shows up Saturday.
Head counter. Notices exactly who hasn't said a word all week.

cards.mask: looks like a group chat meme; measures circle size (T04: Close Friends list vs Mayor of every group chat) and how much contact you need to see (T02)

friend.prompt: In the main group chat, {name} is the one who…

a.t: Adds new people and books the plans.

b.t: Screenshots it all to two favorites.

cards.prompt: Your person says, totally casual: "Let's swap phone passcodes. Nothing's wrong. It just feels close."
cards.teenPrompt: Your best friend says, totally casual: "Let's swap phone passcodes. Nothing's wrong. It's a best friend thing."

options.t: Type mine into their phone before they finish the sentence.
Offer live location instead. The passcode stays mine.
Keep mine. "Ask me anything, anytime. I'll answer."
Laugh, change the subject, hope it never comes back.
Not my call. Parents or work set my phone rules.

cards.mask: looks like a phone privacy question; measures whether closeness means sharing everything or keeping your own door (R1) and phone openness (T01)

friend.prompt: {name}'s person suggests swapping phone passcodes. Nothing's wrong. What does {name} do?

cards.prompt: The second they said "swap passcodes", what showed up first?

options.t: Warm. They want all of me.
Suspicious. Wait, why now? What happened?
Trapped. Saying no now would look guilty.
Cringe. This is a lot.
Curious. What's even on their phone?

cards.mask: looks like a vibe check; logs the emotion under the passcode choice (emotion only, no profile evidence), so 'said yes but felt trapped' can surface as a split

cards.prompt: Think of the last time something was eating at you after midnight. Where did it go first?

options.t: Typed it all out to an AI. It asked good questions.
Voice-noted my closest person. Four minutes, no summary.
Posted something vague and waited to see who'd ask.
Notes app. A whole essay nobody will ever read.
Nowhere. Slept on it. It was smaller by morning.

cards.mask: looks like a late-night habit; measures whether an AI counts as a real confidant (T03), whether you wait to be reached (T02B), and whether your inner world goes to your people or stays with you (R1)

friend.prompt: Something's eating at {name} after midnight. Where does it go first?

b.t: A long voice note to their closest person.

cards.prompt: A new app promises to run your whole week: reminders, plans, even texts. First it wants your contacts, photos, calendar and location.

options.t: Tap Allow on everything without reading. Tap, tap, tap, done.
Read the entire privacy policy first. Yes, all of it.
Allow all, then revoke everything at 2am after one scary video.
Sign up with a fake name and my spare email.
School or work makes me use it. No choice.

cards.mask: looks like an app setup; measures how freely you hand over your data for convenience (T01), with reading the fine print as slight rule-following evidence (T25A)

friend.prompt: A new app wants {name}'s contacts, photos and location. What does {name} do?

a.t: Taps Allow on everything without reading.

b.t: Signs up with a fake name and spare email.

cards.prompt: You and an old close friend haven't texted in four months. Nobody's mad. You still love them.

options.t: Totally fine. Next hangout, we pick up mid-sentence.
Kind of stings. Someone should've texted. Them.

cards.mask: looks like a friendship hot take; measures whether a quiet friendship still feels safe or needs someone to reach out (T02)

friend.prompt: {name} and an old close friend haven't texted in four months. How does {name} feel?

cards.prompt: Someone you talked to for four minutes at a party sends you a follow request.

options.t: Accept. We're basically friends now.
Leave it pending. Forever.

cards.mask: looks like a social media reflex; measures how wide you let your circle go (T04)

friend.prompt: Someone {name} met for four minutes at a party sends a follow request. What does {name} do?

cards.prompt: You owe someone a real apology. You know exactly what you mean. AI could word it way better.

options.t: Let AI polish it. The sorry is still mine.
Send my own clumsy version, typos and all.

cards.mask: looks like a tech opinion; measures whether sincerity lives in the intent and follow-through or in your own raw words (T03)

friend.prompt: {name} owes someone a real apology. AI could word it better. What does {name} send?

b.t: Their own clumsy version, typos and all.

cards.prompt: Your person wants a shared calendar, so you can always see each other's plans.
cards.teenPrompt: Your best friend wants a shared calendar, so you can always see each other's plans.

options.t: Yes. It's color-coded by the end of the night.
Say yes, then never open it again.
Counteroffer: a shared playlist. Same closeness, less schedule.
Pass. Text me and I'll always tell you.

cards.mask: looks like a scheduling app; sealed check for R1 (close means shared vs close still means space)

cards.prompt: You get added to a brand-new group chat. 40 people. You know maybe six.

options.t: Say hi, learn five names, start the first plan.
Screenshot it to my two people: "who ARE these people?"
Mute it before the welcome messages finish loading.
React to everything. Still know nobody by Friday.

cards.mask: looks like group chat chaos; sealed check for the circle-size tag pair (T04)
